messages:
anya: Quick question — we're changing a Gateway + Service binding in terraform PR #487. We switched the Service port name via an annotation, and after apply the pods went Unready in staging for ~20s. Anyone seen this behavior when the Service port name changes?

sam: I have. If a Gateway/Route references the port by name, changing the Service port name can break health-probe resolution until kube finishes reconciling Endpoints/EndpointSlices. What specifically did the PR change?

anya: The module used to set port name `tls-sni`. The PR makes it deterministic based on an infra annotation so it ended up as `tls-sni-v2`. Service snippet (from staging):
```
ports:
- name: tls-sni-v2
  port: 443
  targetPort: 8080
```
Gateway Listener points at port name `tls-sni` previously. The TCPRoute binds to listener port 443.

leo: Short checklist: cluster (staging/prod)? readinessProbe container port vs Service targetPort? GatewayListener references name or number?

anya: Staging. ReadinessProbe uses HTTP GET on containerPort 8080 (/health). Service targetPort is 8080. GatewayListener references port by name in YAML (was `tls-sni`).

irene: Kube resolves named targetPorts at object creation, but other controllers (Gateway API) reference port name at runtime. If the Service port name changes, Gateway API listeners that reference the old name won't match until you update the Gateway. Meanwhile probes from the LB may hit the Service port and expect the same mapping. Transient NotReady makes sense.

sam: Also watch for Terraform recreates — if the Service is replaced rather than patched, endpoints will be lost briefly. Did the TF diff show a replace?

anya: Yes, terraform planned replace for the Service because the port name field changed. We applied and saw a short NotReady window. No errors in Gateway controller logs, just healthcheck failures.

leo: Two mitigation ideas: keep port name stable (preferred) OR update Gateway to reference numeric port instead of name during rollout, and coordinate so both match. Numeric is less brittle for this particular change.

kai: Quick workaround if you must change name: create a second Service port entry with the old name pointing at same targetPort (k8s allows multiple ports). Eg:
```
ports:
- name: tls-sni
  port: 443
  targetPort: 8080
- name: tls-sni-v2
  port: 444
  targetPort: 8080
```
But that complicates Gateway listener mapping. Might be simpler to keep the original name and add an annotation instead.

irene: Also consider terraform lifecycle block to avoid replace on metadata annotation changes if the annotation alone shouldn't trigger a recreate. Or use kubernetes_manifest with patchStrategy to preserve ports.

anya: Good notes. For the PR I'm going to: 1) revert the port-name change so Service.name stays `tls-sni`, 2) update module docs to warn that port name changes are a recreate, 3) open a follow-up to add an explicit migration path (dual-port svc or gateway numeric binding).

sam: :thumbsup: If you want I can run a canary apply in staging after you revert to validate.

anya: Thanks — please do. One more question: should we add an infra-monitoring alert if a Service gets replaced (to catch accidental name flips)?

leo: Definitely. Alert on `k8s.service.created` events with port diffs or a custom metric from kube-event-exporter. Also a short runbook: rollback or rebind Gateway to numeric temporarily.

deploy-bot: apply plan for pr/487 completed in staging — 0 changes pending

anya: Ran the canary apply after the revert. Staging pods no longer flapped. Prod window planned tomorrow with a short maintenance note and rollback plan. Will add the monitoring alert and docs. Thanks all :rocket:
